Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

thus adverb

in this way, like this

also like this, like that, in this way, in that way, this is how, so (in this way)

classical

Cic. Fam. 2.15.2: sed quid agās? sīc vīvitur
Plaut. Bacch. 675: sīc hoc digitulīs duōbus sūmēbās prīmōribus? (“were you picking it up like this, with two fingertips?”)

sīc

adverb

thus, so, in this way; like this

Points back to what was just said, or, with a gesture, to what the speaker shows: “like this” (Lewis & Short: colloquial, mostly in comedy). As an answer, sīc est is “that’s right”.

Other words

  • ita — so, thus, in such a way

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 7.8.4: factum est ita (Lewis & Short); Ter. And. 192: Ita ajunt (“so they say”)

    The same “so”, but most often with a clause to follow: ita … ut, so … that. Alone as an answer it is “yes”.

Examples

  • sīc igitur vīvitur: cotīdiē aliquid legitur aut scrībitur

    so this is how we live: every day something is read or writtenCic. Fam. 9.26.3

  • sed quid agās? sīc vīvitur

    but what can you do? That’s lifeCic. Fam. 2.15.2

  • quod hodiē nōn est, crās erit: sīc vīta trūditur

    what isn’t here today will be here tomorrow: that’s how life pushes onPetr. 45.1

See also therefore, that’s right, yes.
